evidence.text: 元 row: py yuán; MC ngjwon; OC *[ŋ]o[r] (< nasal + uvular); gloss ‘head; first’; GSR 0257a. Compared within this table, the two forms share the reconstructed onset and similar rhyme material, while 玩 has an added suffix. This is compatible with the traditional phonetic analysis but does not alone prove it.

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry reports the received Shuowen explanation as ‘弄也。从玉，元聲’ and records an alternate graph written with 貝. It cites the Warring States poet Qu Yuan’s ‘惜吾不及古人兮，吾誰與玩此芳草’ for an appreciative/handling sense, and quotes the Yijing tradition for 玩 meaning to study or become familiar with. These citations evidence old literary uses but the entry does not date the first attestation of 玩 or establish a stepwise semantic chronology.
evidence.title: A02555 玩 — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 說文釋形; 字樣說明
evidence.text: The entry contrasts the Great Xu edition’s ‘从玉，元聲’ with Duan Yucai’s ‘从王，元聲’; it also says the right side is written as 元. The available textual evidence supports 玉/王 as an editorial or textual difference in description, but no ancient inscription image for 玩 was inspected here, so no graphic chronology or corruption claim is established.
evidence.title: A02555 玩 — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Multi-function Chinese Character Database
evidence.field: 元; 形義通解; 甲骨文、金文、小篆
evidence.text: The database analyzes early 元 as a person with a marked head, with the mark variously a dot, square, or simplified stroke; it describes later small-seal and regular forms as developing from these shapes. It reports oracle-bone uses for beginning/first and place names, and bronze uses for first, beginning, great, and rank. It also notes scholarly disagreement over whether the upper strokes represent 上, favoring the marked-head interpretation. This concerns 元 itself, not an ancient name of a depicted object or the proven shape history of 玩.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 元

evidence.source: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Multi-function Chinese Character Database
evidence.field: 元; 說文; 廣韻; 中古音
evidence.text: This entry gives Shuowen 元 as ‘始也。从一从兀’ and reports a distinct Duan Yucai analysis ‘从一，兀聲’. It lists Guangyun fanqie 愚袁 and the Middle Chinese categories 疑母, level tone, 山攝, 元 rhyme, 合口, third division. These records establish readings/descriptions of 元; they do not themselves establish its phonetic role in 玩.

gaps: The exact Unicode Unihan records for U+73A9 and U+5143 could not be inspected externally because the requested official pages were inaccessible. Local Unihan rows exist and were directly checked: 玩 wán and 元 yuán. The provided error should therefore be described as failed external lookup, not a missing local kMandarin value.

The local Baxter–Sagart table rows were directly checked, but an accessible upstream table page was not verified. Keep the local row provenance explicit; do not present an external source as having verified these readings.

No 玩 oracle-bone, bronze, or seal glyph was visually inspected in this research. The consulted primary-derived dictionary evidence supports the Shuowen analysis and the dictionary records alternate textual descriptions, but the graph’s pre-Shuowen graphic development, any corruption hypothesis, and earliest dated inscription remain unresolved.

The MOE entry supplies literary citations and later dictionary senses, but this research does not establish the chronology or complete semantic links among handling, play, study/contemplation, taunting, and ‘plaything/curio’. The gloss sequence should not be treated as a semantic timeline.

No evidence establishes a jade toy as the original referent, and no whole-graph phonetic loan is proposed. For the internal 元 sound component, its early depicted referent is not needed to posit the traditional phonetic analysis; the component’s ancient sound role is nevertheless not independently demonstrated by modern Mandarin readings alone.

The glyph selections/captions referenced by the review were not included in the supplied packet, so this research could not verify or revise the particular selection or its rights. The official dictionary displays historical glyph records, but no glyph asset licensing terms were inspected; no reuse permission is claimed.
Search activity remained within the bounded plan: three distinct queries, with no additional targeted pass justified by evidence requiring resolution.
